test_added: .sandcastle/plan.test.mts: 12 cases pin the window parse — `off for steps 1–4 (#141)` → parity {issue:141, steps:[1,2,3,4]}, one-step range, no-window ⇒ null, a fenced example ignored, and refusals for backwards, worded, no-range, past-the-last-step and unnamed sections, plus windowStateRefusal(issue, open) and the printed `window:` line. .sandcastle/main.test.mts: 3 cases run `main.mts --plan` against a stubbed gh — open window printed and exit 0, closed window refused with `refused: … #117 … does not report open` and no branch line, no-window issue makes no state query.
concerns: plan.mts:360-369 validates only the range's top end: `off for steps 0–2 (#141)` parses to {issue:141, steps:[0,1,2]} with no refusal, though ADR-0022:39 and docs/agents/sandcastle.md:79 say a step the issue does not have is a refusal; plan.mts:367 also takes the first `#N` anywhere in the section instead of the `(#N)` on the range line, so a prose reference before it becomes the window's owner and is the issue whose open state main checks.

main.mts:230 (the run path's windowStop) is untested: replacing it with `null` leaves `node --test .sandcastle/*.test.mts` at 148/148 — only the --plan call site can go red, so the guard that stops a real run has no test holding it.
